research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's own guide: write a full scene description the way you would brief a photographer (subject, action, setting, light, camera), not a list of keywords
https://dev.to/googleai/getting-the-most-out-of-nano-banana-2-502k — Google AI dev post: Nano Banana 2 is Gemini 3.1 Flash Image; generate options, pick the best composition, then upscale

https://runware.ai/docs/models/google-nano-banana-2/guides/prompting — practitioner guide: put composition and camera specifics early; name the lens and the film stock to get away from the clean default look

https://www.rideapart.com/articles/300448/police-escort-safety-motorcade-honda/ — the Met's Special Escort Group: outriders ride ahead and stop traffic at junctions so the escorted car can pass, with discreet blue lights and whistles
https://www.policeconduct.gov.uk/node/5878 — IOPC case: SEG riders use hand and arm signals and whistle blasts at junctions, so a raised gloved palm is accurate

https://www.england.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/ambulance-vehicle-specification-and-key-considerations.pdf — the NHS England double-crewed ambulance spec: white wipe-clean box body behind a van cab

https://archive.commercialmotor.com/article/30th-june-2005/63/emergency-stops — UK box-body ambulances have a solid bulkhead with a small sliding window (and blind) through to the cab, so the forward view from the back is a framed hatch, as in the reference photo

https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/prehospital-and-disaster-medicine/article/effect-of-operator-position-on-the-quality-of-chest-compressions-delivered-in-a-simulated-ambulance/4416F3962CC1C718D995ED7CCD62315D — in the back, the clinician doing compressions stands or kneels unbelted beside the stretcher while the other is seated at the head

https://britishcinematographer.co.uk/stephen-murphy-bsc-isc-blue-lights/ — BBC's Blue Lights (Belfast police drama): rain FX and wetdowns plus moving coloured lights outside the vehicle to sell night realism

https://britishcinematographer.co.uk/?p=109268 — ambulance-interior drama lighting: cold, sickly interior, rotating lights and flags outside the windows standing in for streetlights and the beacons, keep one healthy skin tone to grade to
https://www.litepanels.com/en/applications/how-to-light-a-car-scene-at-night/ — night car interiors: shape the environment rather than front-lighting faces; dashboard glow as a motivated face light
attach_reference: yes for prompts 1 and 3, no for prompt 2 — those two look through the patient compartment, where the photo's real white cupboards, teal seat and hatch window are what makes it read as a UK ambulance and not a US rig; but the photo is daylight with the hatch open onto a sunny street, so each prompt has to overwrite the light, weather and the view. Prompt 2 is set in the cab, which the photo barely shows, so attaching it would mostly drag in the daylight and the signage.
notes: If any lettering appears on the outrider's jacket, the signage stickers from the reference, or the monitor screen, blur it in the edit. The blue strobe is better added or pumped in the edit as a flicker than trusted to one still. Prompt 3 was written for the red light flooding the whole interior; if it comes back too evenly red, a fast cut from it to a cool-lit shot gives the jolt.

prompts.idea: Frame within a frame: over the kneeling paramedic's shoulder, through the small bulkhead hatch, to the outrider beyond. Three layers of depth show what is being lost and what is stopping it.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 film still at night, from inside the back of a UK ambulance, looking forward. Foreground, out of focus: the shoulder and surgical-masked profile of a female paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and blue gloves, twisted toward the front, mid-compressions over a grey-faced older man in an oxygen mask on a black strapped stretcher. Middle: white cupboards, a teal seat, and the small sliding hatch window into the cab, where the driver's hands grip the wheel. Through the hatch and the rain-streaked windscreen beyond: a red traffic light and a police motorcycle outrider in a hi-vis jacket and helmet, gloved palm raised flat at them. Hard cold strip light, green monitor glow, blue strobe on wet glass. 35mm, grain, underexposed, handheld. No readable text. Thanks.

prompts.idea: In the cab, low between the seats on a wide lens: the driver's white-knuckled hands and the wiper mid-sweep fill the bottom; the outrider stands close in the headlight wash, almost touching the bumper. Puts the viewer in the driver's seat for the fury.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic night still from the cab of a UK ambulance, camera low between the two front seats, wide 24mm lens. Bottom of frame: the driver's hands strangling the steering wheel, knuckles pale, a sleeve of a plain dark-green uniform. The dashboard glows faintly. Top two-thirds: a windscreen streaming with rain, one wiper caught mid-sweep. Just beyond the bonnet, lit hard by the ambulance's headlights, a police motorcycle outrider in a soaked hi-vis jacket and white helmet stands astride his bike, one gloved hand held up flat, visor down, unmoved. Above him a red traffic light blooms through the wet glass, sodium-orange streetlamps smeared behind, blue emergency light flickering across the rain drops. Shot on 35mm film, heavy grain, underexposed, slightly tilted handheld. No readable text, no logos. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Long lens down the whole length of the compartment from the back doors: both masked paramedics turned toward the front, the patient between them, and the red light from the tiny hatch flooding the white interior red. The stop happens to the whole room.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 film still at night, telephoto 85mm view down the full length of a UK ambulance's patient compartment, shot from by the rear doors. Near the bottom, soft: the feet of an older man under a pale blanket on a black strapped stretcher. Mid-frame: two paramedics in plain dark-green uniforms, surgical masks and blue gloves, a man and a woman, both frozen and turned to stare forward, one hand still pressed to the patient's chest. At the far end, small and sharp: the bulkhead hatch window, and through it the rain-blurred windscreen, a red traffic light and a hi-vis police outrider with one gloved hand raised. The red light spills in and stains the white walls and cupboards red, cut by a blue strobe. Green monitor glow. 35mm grain, crushed shadows, handheld. No readable text. Thanks.
